title: logit internals
description: logit observing itself (docs/design/internal-telemetry.md, ADR `internal-telemetry-as-pipeline-events`) alongside the demo's synthetic web traffic. Provisioned by demo/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/dashboards.yaml.

panels.title: web.requests (nginx)
panels.description: Requests reaching the nginx tier -- real visits plus a background synthetic loop -- by status code, proving syslog_in -> json -> scale -> kv_metrics -> keep -> aggregate end to end. Filtered on service.name so this and the haproxy panel beside it don't double-count the shared web.requests measurement.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "web.requests")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["service.name"] == "nginx")
  |> group(columns: ["status"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: web.requests (haproxy)
panels.description: The same web.requests measurement as the nginx panel beside it, filtered to HAProxy's own service.name tag instead -- haproxy_metrics (demo/logit.yaml) is the front door's own request count, upstream of nginx's.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "web.requests")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["service.name"] == "haproxy")
  |> group(columns: ["status"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: web.request_time (nginx, p50 / p99)
panels.description: Milliseconds, not seconds -- nginx_scale (demo/logit.yaml) converts nginx's own $request_time before nginx_metrics ever reads it, so this shares a unit and a measurement with haproxy's panel beside it.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "web.request_time")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "p50" or r._field == "p99")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["service.name"] == "nginx")

panels.title: web.request_time (haproxy, p50 / p99)
panels.description: HAProxy's %Tr is native milliseconds, so haproxy_metrics needs no scale step -- unlike nginx's panel beside it, this reads request_time_ms directly.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "web.request_time")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "p50" or r._field == "p99")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["service.name"] == "haproxy")

panels.title: web.connections_active (haproxy)
panels.description: HAProxy's own process-wide concurrent-connection gauge (%ac, demo/haproxy/haproxy.cfg), riding on each request event -- one series per request/response tag combination rather than one true process-wide series, so this groups everything together and takes the last value seen per window instead of plotting the raw per-tag series (docs/adr/scale-transform.md's sibling reasoning doesn't cover this; see haproxy_metrics's own comment in demo/logit.yaml).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "web.connections_active")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value")
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)

panels.title: logit.component.events.{sent,received,dropped}
panels.description: The uniform per-component runtime instrumentation every component gets for free (Fanout::send / run_transform / run_output).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "logit.component.events.sent" or r._measurement == "logit.component.events.received" or r._measurement == "logit.component.events.dropped")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value")
  |> group(columns: ["_measurement", "component"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)

from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "logit.component.process.duration")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "p99")
  |> group(columns: ["component"])

from(bucket: "metrics")

panels.title: Loki: raw demo traffic ({service_name="demo-app"})
panels.description: `loki_out` (`otlp_out`, docs/plans/otlp-logs-and-resource-identity.md workstream B) exports app_json's events straight to Loki over OTLP/HTTP -- no relay service in between. `service_name`/`service_namespace` stream labels come from `app_identity` (`set`, ADR operator-declared-resource-attributes) stamping the batch's resource, not from any per-event config field.

panels.title: Loki: 5xx lines/sec (LogQL | json filter)
panels.description: LogQL parsing the JSON message body itself, not just matching stream labels -- `| json` extracts `status` from each line, then filters on it.

panels.title: Tempo: logit's own internal spans
panels.description:
logit observing itself as *traces*, not just metrics (docs/adr/internal-span-emission-and-deterministic-sampling.md, docs/plans/otlp-end-to-end.md) -- one span per node-visit (listener send, transform process/flush, sink deliver), exported over OTLP/gRPC by demo/logit.yaml's `tempo_out`. Click a trace ID to open its waterfall and see the pipeline's real shape: a syslog_in root with json/scale/kv_metrics/keep/aggregate children, or an internal-only root for `self`'s own drain. Scoped to `{resource.service.name="logit"}` -- as of docs/adr/trace-context-span-lifting.md, `tempo_out` also carries haproxy's/nginx's real access-line spans (see the panel below), so `{}` would now mix the two.

This is a `table` panel, not a `traces` panel: Grafana's `traces` panel type renders one trace's waterfall, not a searchable list of many -- the Tempo datasource's own response tells Grafana as much (`preferredVisualisationType: "table"`), and each row's Trace ID is already a link into the full trace view.

panels.title: Tempo: demo request traces (haproxy -> nginx -> app)
panels.description: The real per-request trace this demo exists to show (docs/adr/trace-context-span-lifting.md, docs/OVERVIEW.md's "see a request pass through the stack, server to server to app"): haproxy mints the trace, both haproxy and nginx contribute a real span derived from their own access log line by `trace_context`'s `span:` block, and `demo-app` contributes a real OpenTelemetry span sent straight to Tempo (never through `logit` -- see demo/logit.yaml's header comment). Scoped to `{resource.service.name="haproxy"}`, the trace's root, so this table and the one above never overlap.

panels.title: logit.internal.spans.dropped (buffer_full)
panels.description: The per-component span buffer's overflow counter (MAX_SPANS_PER_COMPONENT, docs/design/internal-telemetry.md) -- should stay at zero at demo volume; a nonzero value means the demo's traffic is outrunning the bounded buffer between `internal`'s drain ticks, not that traces are being lost silently.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "metrics")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "logit.internal.spans.dropped")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value")
  |> group(columns: ["component", "reason"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: sum, createEmpty: false)
